scenes.headline: How a certificate proves a 3D solve is optimal
scenes.sub: Five 3D releases this week, and what a reader can check
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Vernier! Five 3D reconstruction papers landed this week. The most unusual one does not just solve for the camera. It proves the answer is the best one.

scenes.text: XM4D turns camera motion and object motion into two convex relaxations, and a certificate tells you when the answer is the global optimum.
scenes.mark: a certificate tells you when the answer is the global optimum
scenes.say: The idea: turn both halves of the problem into convex relaxations, and check a certificate that says when the answer is the global optimum.

steps.say: Point trackers and a depth model turn the video into tracks lifted to 3D, split into static and moving points.
The static tracks become a bundle adjustment over scaled rotations, solved as a relaxation with a certificate.
With the cameras fixed, moving points ride a graph of nodes. Their rotations are solved the same certified way.
Only then does Gaussian splatting refine how the scene looks.

scenes.title: Local search vs a certified solve

left.title: Local search
items: Can stop at a wrong rotation
left.say: A local solver starts from a guess and can stop at a wrong answer without knowing it.

right.title: Certified relaxation
items: Raises the rank until it certifies
right.say: The staircase raises the rank until the certificate holds, and when the relaxation is tight, the answer is provably optimal.

steps.say: In the paper's figure, the local solver leaves some graph nodes with flipped rotations, boxed in orange.

scenes.title: Trainspotting: pose AUC@30 on held-out objects
scenes.note: Recomputed from the released per-sample results
scenes.say: The one paper you can check end to end is Trainspotting. Its released per-sample results recompute to the same table: eighty-one against twenty-five for the model it started from.

scenes.text: A certificate covers the solve, not its inputs: wrong depth or tracks still give a certified wrong answer.
scenes.mark: covers the solve, not its inputs
scenes.say: Remember: a certificate covers the solve, not its inputs. Feed it wrong depth or wrong tracks and it certifies the wrong problem.

recap: Trainspotting's table recomputes from released rows
The certificate covers the solve, not the inputs
scenes.say: Certified cameras and motion, a dataset you can check, and a certificate that only covers the solve.
